limitations.title: Implicit Feedback from Reviews Only
limitations.description: Interactions are derived exclusively from Steam user reviews (is_recommended). Users write reviews for games they actively chose to purchase/play, meaning the dataset lacks explicit negative impressions from non-purchasers.

limitations.title: Popularity and Selection Bias
limitations.description: Highly popular titles receive a disproportionate volume of interactions. Baseline models and retrieval stages exhibit popularity bias towards top catalog items unless explicitly counterbalanced.

limitations.title: Per-User Temporal Split Protocol
limitations.description: The split uses a per-user chronological partition: for each user, their latest positive review forms the test target, their second-to-latest forms the validation target, and all preceding reviews form the training history. This evaluates next-item prediction per user rather than a single global time cutoff.

limitations.title: Item Universe Selection from Full Period
limitations.description: Catalog inclusion in the 3,000-game universe is determined using total positive counts across all periods. This is an accepted design trade-off to ensure stable item features.

limitations.title: Single Held-Out Item Target
limitations.description: Each evaluation user has exactly one held-out target item in val and test. Consequently, Hit Rate @ k and Recall @ k are equivalent indicators.

limitations.title: Offline Metrics vs Online Performance
limitations.description: Offline ranking gains (NDCG@10, HR@10) reflect retrieval of historical positive reviews, but do not prove online user satisfaction, serendipity, or real-world purchase conversion.

limitations.title: Simulated Cold-Start Evaluation
limitations.description: The cold-start study simulates new items at inference time by replacing learned ID embeddings with the unknown-item token and zeroing CF scores. Item content projections (MiniLM, tags) were trained on the catalog features, so this is a simulation rather than a prospective trial.

limitations.title: Dev-Profile Scale Constraints
limitations.description: The dev profile operates on 5000 evaluation users and 3,000 items. Full production deployment covers hundreds of thousands of users and games.

limitations.title: Test Split Metric Shift
limitations.description: Across all models, test metrics (e.g. NDCG@10 0.0535 vs 0.0630) are lower than validation metrics. This reflects genuine temporal drift: the held-out test review is each user's most recent interaction, often occurring months after training interactions.

limitations.title: All-Time Item Statistics & Temporal Cutoff
limitations.description: Item statistics (user_reviews count, positive_ratio) are all-time aggregations computed through 2022 and can include interactions after a user's chronological split cutoff point.

limitations.title: Cold-Start Evaluation & Popularity Proxy Leakage
limitations.description: Evaluation on the 437 simulated new-item users (random 10% items, seed 42) with the seed-42 Two-Tower artifact yields: (a) unmasked: HR@10=0.0618, NDCG@10=0.0317, n=437; (b) ID masked: HR@10=0.0641, NDCG@10=0.0314, n=437; (c) ID masked + train_positives = raw 0: HR@10=0.0000, NDCG@10=0.0000, n=437; (c2) ID masked + train_positives = standardized catalog mean (z=0): HR@10=0.0023, NDCG@10=0.0011, n=437; (c3) as (c2) + user_reviews & positive_ratio at standardized catalog mean: HR@10=0.0023, NDCG@10=0.0010, n=437. The legacy score 0.0732 was not reproduced under any valid condition (documented as not reproduced, hypothesis: legacy un-neutralized popularity proxy / unmasked interaction leakage).

limitations.title: Ranker Evaluation Discrepancy Analysis (0.0501 vs 0.0622)
limitations.description: The earlier 0.0501 test NDCG@10 observed in preliminary experiment harnesses vs the official pipeline 0.0622 was investigated. Because exploratory test history was truncated, the exact code difference cannot be isolated to a single commit; the validated hypothesis is that earlier harnesses evaluated test candidates without appending the validation target item to the user fold-in history, causing a ~40% candidate pool miss rate. Official evaluate_model(split='test') evaluates on full fold-in history.

limitations.title: LightGBM Ranker Determinism & Reproducibility
limitations.description: LightGBM LambdaMART ranker training is configured with deterministic=True and force_row_wise=True to guarantee bitwise reproducibility across runs with the same random seed. Multi-threaded training on seed 45 and seed 46 achieves bitwise identical validation and test metrics across multiple fresh process runs.

limitations.title: Ablation Confidence Intervals & Multiplicity
limitations.description: Bootstrap confidence intervals for architectural and feature-group ablations are computed pairwise at the nominal 95% level and are not adjusted for multiple comparisons.

limitations.title: Single-Seed Ablation Interpretability
limitations.description: Single-seed ablations are indicative only; multi-seed evaluations are recommended to distinguish marginal feature effects from optimization and sampling variance.

limitations.title: Catalog Coverage Definition (Masked vs Unmasked)
limitations.description: Official catalog coverage@10 (0.3597 test for Two-Tower) is strictly computed after masking out items already seen in the user's fold-in history (-inf). If computed on unmasked raw scores, coverage appears higher (0.4373) because models repetitively recommend already-consumed items. Seen-item masking is essential for production serving.
